note: PARTIAL RESTORATION. The original 37-step manual script was lost with its session workspace and had never been committed. Steps below were recovered from the project knowledge base on 2026-08-22 by their recorded IDs and outcomes. Group sizes from the last register are kept in `originalCount` so the shortfall stays visible. No step text has been invented to fill a gap — a fabricated step is worse than a missing one.
rule: NEVER mark a step verified without actually doing it. This was violated once (email recorded as 'confirmed' on the strength of a test that only checked the notify call fired; no inbox was ever opened) and it is the single easiest way to make the whole register worthless.

steps.step: Sign in to production as Levi with his real password.
steps.proves: Real-auth behaviour, which no automated check can reach.
steps.blockedBy: LEVI ONLY — needs his password. Cannot be delegated to a session.

steps.step: Load the app at a genuine phone viewport in Levi's own browser.
steps.proves: The mobile layout on his real device, not an emulated one.
steps.blockedBy: The browser bridge cannot resize his window.

steps.step: Cross-check every number in the morning brief against the database.
steps.proves: The brief states counts that match the records, and does not contradict its own tiles.
steps.history: Failed twice. MF-1 pass 1 fixed model fabrication, which was not the cause; pass 2 found assemble() defined the approval queue over ALL items instead of open ones, sweeping in work already done. needsReview 8 → 2.

steps.step: Pin a card in Needs review to Top 3, then reconcile the column counts.
steps.proves: One record renders as exactly one card, and the columns sum to the open item count.
steps.history: Fixed PR #28. Status column wins; Top 3 draws from Backlog and In progress only, and prints '★ N pinned items are in Needs review' so the star does not look broken.

steps.step: Compare the brief's open/review counts against what the browser shows.
steps.proves: Client-generated recurring occurrences are not silently missing from the brief.
steps.history: Server reports 19 open / 2 review against the browser's 20 / 3. The extra item is a recurring occurrence the client materialises locally and never persists, so the brief structurally cannot see it. Needs its own fix: persist generated occurrences, or have the brief generate them the same way the client does.

steps.step: Speak a task and check what Wingman structured out of it.
steps.proves: Voice capture produces a usable task, and capVia records voice only when speech recognition actually produced words.

steps.step: Route a real task to Wingman and read the draft it produces.
steps.proves: The draft is the deliverable itself — no plan section, no 'let me research', no inter-tool narration.

steps.step: Work the review lane on real drafts: approve, edit, redo with a note, skip.
steps.proves: Approve-then-advance works, and a redo note actually outranks the card.

steps.step: Run a trip end to end: plan, attach to the card, export the calendar file, create the mission.
steps.proves: The travel path produces a booking brief a human can act on, with no invented fares or confirmations.

groups.title: Read it as a person would

steps.step: Open Goals and try to do what the page tells you to do.
steps.proves: The page does not instruct an action it does not provide.
steps.history: Goals said 'link tasks so this goal can track itself' while offering only New goal / Update / Edit. Logged as X31, then fixed.

steps.step: Load the app cold and watch the Wingman badge on first paint.
steps.proves: The badge does not flash a wrong number before correcting itself.
steps.history: Shows 0 on first paint, corrects to 4 after navigating. Observed twice; never isolated further.

steps.step: Walk the five destinations on a real iPhone.
steps.proves: Every destination is reachable on a phone. The bottom bar has always been wider than a phone; PR #32 made it scroll horizontally as a STOPGAP.
steps.openQuestion: Which five items belong on a phone. A horizontally-scrolling bottom bar is not an answer.

groups.title: Did it actually do the thing in the world

steps.step: Send the brief to a real address and OPEN THE INBOX.
steps.proves: Email is actually delivered — not that the call fired.
steps.history: POST /api/brief?send=1 returns HTTP 200 with ok:false and 'You can only send testing emails to your own email address'. The Resend account is in test mode. The 6:30am brief, every assignment notification and every invite have been failing silently for as long as they have existed. Three code paths affected: api/brief.js, api/notify.js, api/send.js.
steps.fix: LEVI ONLY — add dvlmnt.com at resend.com/domains, add the SPF/DKIM records at the registrar, wait for Verified, then set RESEND_FROM in Vercel and redeploy.
steps.lesson: This step sat unrun longer than any other, and it was the most consequential finding of the whole exercise. No automated test could have caught it: the code is correct and the API returns 200.

steps.step: Trigger a push notification and confirm it arrives on the phone.
steps.proves: Phone alerts work. Requires the Home Screen install on iPhone.

steps.step: Wait for the 6:30am cron and check the inbox.
steps.proves: The scheduled brief is delivered, and brief_sends logs the outcome.
steps.note: The first real proof will report a FAILURE because of X18. That is the send-log feature working, not breaking.

steps.step: Assign a task to Wingman and follow where it goes.
steps.proves: Routing work makes a count rise somewhere the user can see.
steps.history: 'Order garage lightbulbs' appeared to vanish. It had not — Queue → Backlog → Needs review, with a good draft. Nothing told him. #ol2RevN was a span hard-coded display:none that updateCounts() wrote into on every render. Now a real ▸ Needs review row with an amber count.

steps.step: Make a draft call fail and see what the task does.
steps.proves: A failed draft is recorded and offered a retry, instead of leaving the task silently in Backlog.
steps.history: draftFor() had no else branch. Now records aiStatus:'failed' plus the error, toasts, and the next-step bar leads with 'Wingman stalled' offering ▸ Try again and Take it myself.

steps.step: Sign in as Zoe and establish what a non-admin can actually see and do.
steps.proves: The member experience. Both current users are admin, so this has never been exercised.
steps.note: Until this runs, every statement about what a member can do is design intent, not observation.

steps.step: Delete the old GitHub personal access token.
steps.proves: A credential that should not still exist does not.
